biography.ja: 現在のスロヴェニアに生まれ、ウィーンで学んだ。音楽評論家としてはワーグナー派の急先鋒としてブラームスを激しく攻撃したことで知られ、当時のウィーン楽壇の党派対立を体現する人物であった。梅毒による病に生涯苦しめられ、精神を病んで精神病院に収容された末、40代前半で世を去った。
biography.en: Born in what is now Slovenia, he studied in Vienna. As a music critic he was known as a fierce partisan of Wagner who attacked Brahms sharply, embodying the factional rivalries of Viennese musical life at the time. He suffered throughout his life from illness caused by syphilis and, his mind deteriorating, was confined to an asylum before dying in his early forties.

style.ja: 詩の言葉の抑揚や意味の陰影を細部まで音楽に映し出す精緻な歌曲書法を確立し、シューベルトから続くドイツ・リートの伝統を新たな高みへ押し上げた。ピアノ伴奏部を単なる伴奏ではなく詩の心理描写を担う対等な声部として扱い、ワーグナーの半音階的和声語法を歌曲という小さな器の中で応用した。
style.en: He established a meticulous song-writing technique that reflected the inflection and shades of meaning of poetic text in fine detail, carrying the German Lied tradition descended from Schubert to a new height. He treated the piano accompaniment not as mere support but as an equal voice conveying the poem's psychology, applying Wagner's chromatic harmonic language within the small vessel of the song.

impact.ja: 生前は批評家としての攻撃的な言動もあってウィーン楽壇で物議を醸したが、歌曲作曲家としてはシューベルトの後継者として高く評価され、特にイタリアの詩を題材とした歌曲集は精緻な詩と音楽の一致の頂点として今なお歌手たちに愛唱されている。ブラームスとの対立は、19世紀後半のウィーンにおける保守派と革新派の分裂を象徴する逸話としてしばしば語られる。
impact.en: In his lifetime his combative behavior as a critic made him a controversial figure in Viennese musical life, but as a song composer he came to be regarded as Schubert's true heir, and his song collections setting Italian-themed poetry in particular remain beloved by singers today as a peak achievement of matching text and music with precision. His rivalry with Brahms is often recounted as emblematic of the split between conservative and progressive factions in late-nineteenth-century Vienna.

en: Wagnerian critic who feuded with Brahms
